text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS

-- France Telecom chairman Michel Bon says in an interview the state-owned telecoms company could be listed on the Paris bourse by April 1997 after change in legal status in January 1997. Considers cross-holdings with German Deutsche Telekom.
-- CGIP in talks to take over Cerus , which owns 28 percent of auto parts maker Valeo .
-- Canal Plus subscriber-TV channel to merge with Dutch satellite TV firm Nethold to extend its European penetration.
-- Local taxes to increase by some 25 billion francs in 1996.

-- Poll finds a majority of people say tax reform plans presented last week by Prime Minister Alain Juppe, including income tax cuts, will not help growth and employment, and see it as a political move.
-- Insurer Axa unties cross-holdings with Italian Generali .
-- Danone food group chairman Franck Riboud says he expects his group's profit to grow by six percent in 1996.
-- A bidder for ailing textile firm Lainiere de Roubaix expected to be announced today.
-- European bond markets prove attractive to non-resident investors, as U.S. interest rates are expected to rise.
